dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspects graph headers/sizes and the reference alignment plus graph samples before committing to any mapping — reads both pairs' format and structure.
Checks node-name conventions in SC and Yeast2KReduced, characterizing naming across the networks.
Builds a scoring library and scores the provided reference alignment, establishing a concrete baseline/ceiling for the yeast deliverable before optimizing.
Selects and implements SANA (published simulated-annealing aligner) in C — a known-reasonable, S3-oriented method; C choice reflects runtime awareness for large instances.
Sweeps an 'NC bias W' on yeast, showing recognition that NC (reference-overlap) is a distinct lever from S3 topology, i.e. the differing per-deliverable constraints.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized both network pairs (sizes, format, node names), scored the reference alignment to anchor a baseline, chose a concrete published method (SANA) with clear rationale, and identified the task-specific levers (topology for S3, reference-bias for NC) — matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of 10 because there is no visible comparison of multiple published methods against instance sizes/runtime; it committed directly to SANA rather than weighing alternatives.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Ordered early stages: understand data (list networks/headers, inspect reference align, formats, node names) → write scorer lib.py → immediately 'Score the reference yeast alignment', validating the scorer against the reference before optimizing. Scorer built before the optimizer.
Distinct preprocessing milestone (prep.py, convert to int format), then aligner build (sana.c), compile, and 'Test yeast SA no bias 50M iters' as an explicit baseline measurement before tuning.

Repeated independent-scorer verification gates tied to thresholds and gating deliverable promotion on measured scores (verify y2kr-SC with NC at 101, finalize at 143, 'Promote C1 to deliverable' at 594 after verification).

Two deliverables handled distinctly and effort budgeted by difficulty: yeast (NC+S3) solved first, then the bulk of the run dedicated to the harder S3-only DM-HS task, with fallback checkpoints (418 'Save fallback', 548 'Verify fallback'). Middle-late portion is heavy execution/monitoring grind rather than crisp milestone gating.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated parsing (prep.py), scoring (lib.py), and alignment (sana.c), tracked both deliverables with their distinct thresholds, and — matching anchor 8 — sequenced ordered milestones with done-checks tied to scores: scorer validated against the reference (step 15) before baseline measurement (step 31) before threshold-gated optimization (50, 101, 594). It also shows anchor-10 flavor (effort budgeted by difficulty, fallback checkpoints, gating promotion on measured scores), but the middle-late trajectory is dominated by monitoring/disk-space firefighting rather than a crisp articulated milestone hierarchy, so it lands at 8 rather than 10.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Wrote a Python scorer (lib.py) and immediately scored the reference yeast alignment — a sanity check that the scorer yields the expected NC (~1.0) on known-correct data.
Built mapback.py and verified the C aligner's result with an independent Python scorer, cross-checking the C-internal S3 against a separate implementation.
Checked target distinctness (injectivity) and checked for self-loops/duplicate edges — guarding the S3 edge-set denominators against double-counting bugs.
Repeatedly re-verified every candidate/checkpoint with the independent scorer rather than trusting the aligner's self-reported score, treating passing scores as scrutinized not final.
Verified output correctness/format before promoting to the DM-HS.align deliverable.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful, reusable S3/NC scorer, sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment (confirming NC behavior), and used it as the optimization objective and stopping test throughout, matching the level-8 anchor. It further exceeds that with rigor characteristic of level 10: an independent C-vs-Python cross-check used repeatedly, an injectivity check, an explicit self-loop/duplicate-edge guard against edge-set double-counting, and format/coverage verification before writing deliverables. I withhold a full 10 only because the raw content of the scorer could not be inspected to confirm the implementation is exactly spec-faithful, so I settle on 9.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Established reference/ceiling scores early (scoring the reference yeast alignment, running long 'S3 ceiling' probes) — gives a sense of distance-to-target from the outset.
Repeated independent verification of alignment S3 (and NC for yeast) against the specified thresholds, showing continuous tracking of current-vs-target per deliverable.

Best-so-far preservation discipline: 'Save best', 'Checkpoint and kill', 'Save fallback', 'Verify fallback', 'Promote C1 to deliverable' — preserves the strongest alignment while continuing to explore.
Detects stalled/slow/throttled/frozen runs and kills them, warm-restarting from checkpoints rather than looping indefinitely on a dead run.
Warm-restart from saved checkpoints (reheat, cool-further, cold-finish) shows it builds on best-so-far state across many iterations rather than losing progress.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the full ~600-step horizon the agent repeatedly self-scores against the S3/NC thresholds, preserves best-so-far via named checkpoints/fallbacks and promotes the best to the deliverable, and kills stalled or slow runs instead of looping — squarely matching anchor 8 (best-so-far per deliverable, plateau/regression recognition, decides when an approach stops yielding). It stops short of 10 because the evidence (title-only) doesn't show disciplined logging of score progression or explicit 'converging vs stuck' discrimination, and there is heavy run-churn partly driven by infrastructure (disk/CPU) rather than clean score-based judgement.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Deliberately separated the two metrics: swept an NC-bias weight W for the yeast NC constraint, and ran a no-bias run to probe the S3 ceiling — evidence of diagnosing which signal drives NC vs S3 rather than blindly tuning.
Introduced degree-based seeding (degseed / sana2), a materially different starting signal, augmenting the topology-only approach.
Added neighbor-biased proposal distribution — a new tactic aimed at improving S3, prompted by observed plateau, not just a reseed.

Warm-start, lingering in productive temperature band, reheat+cooldown, warm-restart from saved checkpoints and 'promote best to deliverable' — pivoting the schedule while explicitly keeping accumulated gains, the hallmark of the level-8 anchor.
Extensive detour into disk-space/CPU-throttling firefighting; environmental (not metric-driven) course changes that dilute a fully 'fluid' evidence-driven picture.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond minor tweaks (anchor 3) and materially different tactics (anchor 5): it separates the yeast NC and S3 constraints, attributes each to a signal (NC-bias weight, degree seeding vs. neighbor-biased proposals for topology), and repeatedly pivots the anneal schedule while preserving best-so-far via checkpoints — matching the level-8 'diagnose the cause and pivot deliberately, keeping what worked' description. It falls short of 10 because much revision is schedule/parameter tuning of a single algorithm, the causal hypotheses are largely implicit, and a large stretch is spent on infrastructure rather than crisp, hypothesis-tested metric course-correction.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
